#### Imports Tab

This tab is not available for dead oil meters or flash gas meters.

The Imports tab contains information about how data should be imported for meters. Setting these options helps streamline the meter import process. For instance, you can specify an import driver and import path (file and folder name) so that you do not have to enter it every time you import meter data. You can also assign auto edits based on known routine occurrences for a meter; FLOWCAL will then make these adjustments automatically.



<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="ScreenShot" style="width: 646;height: 600;" />

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Import Options">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Import Options</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Import Options">

- **Compare to Master Characteristics** - When set to "Yes", FLOWCAL will verify if the meter’s characteristics matches the master characteristics. If the master characteristics are different from the meter characteristics, an exception will generate. Exceptions and updates of master characteristics are managed within the Master Data Validation screen.

- **External Volume** - An external volume meter is usually a meter whose “official measurement” or custody volume is managed by a third party outside of FLOWCAL; data corrections or edits are not expected to take place in the application. Examples of external volumes are chart volumes and third-party measured volumes.

  Data for external volume meters can be imported via normal imports such as CFX files, text files, or Transaction Queue processing, or entered manually.

  Defining a meter as an external volume meter makes the meter available for selection within the External Volume interface.

- **Update Meter Name**\* - When set to "Yes" (default), the meter name is updated on import with the meter name from the field. Set this option to "No" to prevent the meter name from being updated on import.

- **Inhibit Default Exceptions** - When set to "Yes", FLOWCAL will not generate default exceptions. User-configured validations will still generate exceptions.

- **Sync Operational to Contractual** - When set to "Yes", FLOWCAL will update the meter with the contractual limits that have been set on the Master Data Validations screen. This is for items such as calibrations, tests, and samples that are set to standard operating procedures and/or government requirements.

- **Ignore Contract Hour**\* - When set to "Yes", the contract hour will not be updated on file import or through Transaction Queue.

- **PFX Recalc Method** - Recalculation method used on PFX imports. Choose between the standard liquid recalc methods or select “None. Import Prove PDF Only”. The “None. Import Prove PDF Only” option is used by companies who are retroactively recalculating volume and mass in the flow computer and do not want FLOWCAL to calculate a new volume and mass on top of the new one calculated by the flow computer. Only the import of the PDF is performed.

  This feature is only available with the Liquids add-on and requires PROVEit.

- **Flow Computer Product Mapping** - When set to "Yes", the Flow Computer Editor is enabled. The Flow Computer Editor is used when a SCADA system knows which product position is being used for calculations, but not the product name or product code. For example: the SCADA system may be able to tell that the batch flowing is for product position 2, but it does not know what the product is. SCADA will report this position as the product name in the CFX file, rather than a FLOWCAL product code. You can then use the Flow Computer Editor to update the products when the products in the field flow computer are modified.

  This feature is only available with the Liquids add-on.

- **Auto Edit Criteria** - An auto edit (see: [Auto Edits Editor](../../Auto%20Edits/Auto%20Edits%20Editor.md)) can be assigned to the meter to address routine occurrences for that meter. FLOWCAL will automatically make these adjustments on imports or edits. Check the "Apply on Import Only" checkbox to apply the auto edits only when the data is imported.

- **Import ID** - The meter number in the system sending data to FLOWCAL may not match the meter number in FLOWCAL. In this case, defining an Import ID will ensure the data is imported to the appropriate meter.

  When using the Import ID for text file or Transaction Queue imports, the option to use Import ID must be enabled on the Service Configuration screen.

  When importing MBS## files, there is a requirement that the meter name in FLOWCAL match that in the MBS## file. To use a different meter name in FLOWCAL, set the meter name of the meter in the MBS## file in the Import ID field.

  The use of Import ID is supported by text file, Transaction Queue, and Flow Automation MBS## file imports.

  See: [Configure Imports](../../Admin%20Options/Configure%20Imports.md)

- **Proving Import ID** - The meter number in the PROVEit PFX file being imported may not match the meter number in FLOWCAL. In this case, defining a Proving Import ID will ensure the data is imported to the appropriate meter.

  This feature is only available with the Liquids add-on.

- **Periodic Snap/Batch Snap** - These fields are used to snap incoming data to the start of the resolution period (such as the top of the hour for hourly resolution). If a time stamp falls within the range specified, the time stamp will snap to the top of the hour. If multiple records meet time frame criteria, the first record will be flagged at the top of the hour, and the next record will be flagged for one second after (or one second before for time trails data). The adjustment of the time stamp occurs during import, without a revision being created.

  The total of the time before the start of the hour and after the end of the hour cannot exceed the number of seconds specified for data resolution in the meter characteristics (3600 for hourly data, 900 for 15-minute data).

- **Time Zone Shift**\* – Applies only to gas and liquid CFX and text file imports, as well as liquid TFX files. (See: [Date and Time Adjustments During Import](Date%20and%20Time%20Adjustments%20During%20Import.md))

- **DST Shift**\* – Applies only to gas and liquid CFX and text file imports, as well as liquid TFX files. (See: [Date and Time Adjustments During Import](Date%20and%20Time%20Adjustments%20During%20Import.md))

- **Time Leads Shift**\* – Applies only to gas CFX and text file imports (not supported for monthly data resolution). (See: [Date and Time Adjustments During Import](Date%20and%20Time%20Adjustments%20During%20Import.md))

\* These options are not supported by Transaction Queue.

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Pressure Temperature">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Pressure/Temperature Source</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Pressure Temperature">

If a meter does not have associated pressure or temperature, you can use the Pressure/Temperature Source options to assign a source meter to provide its pressure or temperature for calculation purposes.

The pressure and/or temperature must be available on the source meter for it to apply to the destination meter during import. If the data for the source meter is imported after that of the destination meter, the pressure and/or temperature from the source will not be applied.

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="File Options">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />File Options</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="File Options">

- **Driver** - Import driver selection based on the type of file expected during imports. If the driver is not installed, select the button to install the appropriate driver from the Import Driver Editor.

  Most users import CFX files and select the STNDCFX driver.

- **Import Path (Folder)** - Select the import directory or copy/paste the file path from Windows Explorer.

  Windows has a hard-coded limit of 260 characters for file paths; file paths longer than this will not work. Importing files from a local install allows for using drive letters for network file paths; however, Citrix resolves the actual network location, which can cause the number of characters in a file path to exceed this limit.

- **Subfolder or Filename** - Select a subfolder or file name for importing CFX files.
  - Select a subfolder if you are importing CFX files with a datetime stamped file name, as the import file name will be different for every import.
  - Select a file name if you are importing CFX files with a meter ID as the file name, as the import file name will remain constant.

- **Import CFX Units** - When set to "Yes", units specified in the CFX file will be imported.

- **Ignore Configuration Snapshots** - By default, meter configurations specified in a CFX file are imported. CFX meter configurations are automatically associated with the latest flow data record included in the file. At times, the configuration data provided is not in sync with the periodic data and should be ignored. When this option is set to "Yes":
  - Import of meter configuration snapshots will be prevented, including analysis.
  - Meter characteristic records in the Volume Editor need to be updated manually or via events from the flow computer.
  - Meter analysis records in the Volume Editor need to be updated manually, via events from the flow computer, or from analysis provided as part of the History record.

- <span id="CreateRevisions"></span>**Create Revisions** - By default, data imported from CFX will not overwrite existing data. When this option is enabled, if differences are found between the time stamp, differential pressure, pulses, pressure, temperature, volume, or energy values, the data will be imported as a new revision (for closed data, a prior period adjustment will be created). If the data being imported is the same as the existing data, the import will be ignored. This is commonly used to track revisions of third-party data that is not being edited locally and does not have source analysis being applied via a source assignment.

Applying analysis to recalculate the imported volume and energy must be done after all imports for the time frame are complete; subsequent imports will not recalculate based on the quality source data.

- This field is available for gas meters only.

- **Import Alternate Periodics** - By default, alternate periodic information is not imported. Alternate periodic information is generally flow data represented at another resolution. For example, CFX typically will import hourly periodic data. Daily periodic data from the EFM could be provided via the alternate periodic section of CFX. Alternate periodics are stored but not validated or used in any way. Setting this option to "Yes" enables the import of alternate periodic records from CFX imports and allows this data to display in the Volume Editor.

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Conditional Import Rules">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Conditional Import Rules</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Conditional Import Rules">

Conditional import rules are available to allow rejection of data that does not meet specific criteria, such as temperature that is out of range. That hour's record is discarded, but additional records that import with the flagged record are kept.

Conditional import rules are supported for all files types; however, they are not supported for Transaction Queue imports.

</div>
